proofs.text: Call `commit_records(identity="developer")` in a repository with an upstream; verify `git log -1` names the record file and the remote's HEAD moved. Repeat with a record retention deleted and verify the commit carries the deletion. Repeat with no upstream, with no remote, and with the record already at HEAD; verify each prints `no upstream`, `No remote is configured` and `Nothing to commit` respectively and returns without raising

reasons: PROOF-4 happy_path_only: No proof of this rule names a rejection, an error or a boundary.
rule_text: A developer's commit stages the records and the deletions retention made, commits under the developer's own git identity and pushes; with no remote, no upstream or nothing staged it prints the reason and exits 0

tests.body:
def test_a_developer_commit_lands_and_pushes(project, with_remote):
    path = records_module.write_record(project, record(), 'ada@example.com')
    sha = records_module.commit_records(
        project, [path], 'developer', 'purlin: record for 4f1c2ab')

    assert len(sha) == 40
    subject = git(project, 'log', '-1', '--format=%s').stdout.strip()
    assert subject == 'purlin: record for 4f1c2ab'
    listed = git(with_remote, 'ls-tree', '-r', '--name-only', 'main').stdout
    assert path in listed, 'the record did not reach the remote'
tests.name: test_a_developer_commit_carries_the_deletions_retention_made
